transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Yeah, uh… I came in because I just can’t sit still. It’s like I got a motor running inside me all day, you know? Like if I’m at church, or sitting here at the clinic, or even just at home, I start feeling trapped, like I gotta get up or do something.

Even waiting in a chair makes me feel all wound up. I was telling my cousin the other day—well, he don’t really listen much—but it’s like my body wants to move before I even think about it. So… that’s why I’m here.
Have you ever had periods where you felt unusually energetic, needed less sleep, or were more active than usual, even if it was for just a few days?

Uh… I don’t know. I mean, I’m kind of always moving around, so it’s hard for me to tell what’s “more than usual,” you know? Like some days I’ll be up pacing or doing little things, but then I’ll sit down and remember I was supposed to call somebody, and then I end up looking for my shoes—sorry, I’m getting off track.

Less sleep… I don’t really know. I haven’t noticed a stretch like that where I suddenly didn’t need sleep and felt great or anything. I’m just… restless a lot, I guess.
Do you often find it hard to focus on tasks, or do you feel disorganized in your daily activities?

Yeah, focus… yeah, that happens. Like when somebody’s telling me ride times, or what we need from the pantry, or even plans at church, I’ll be listening real good at the start. I’m nodding and everything.

But then my mind just kinda slips off somewhere else, and next thing I know I missed the part I actually needed. Then later I’m like, wait, what time did they say? Or who was bringing what? It gets frustrating, ’cause I don’t mean to ignore people. It just… goes sideways on me.
Do you find yourself moving around, fidgeting, or feeling restless so much during the day that it interferes with what you’re trying to do, like at work or when you’re trying to relax?

Yeah, yeah, that’s… that’s pretty much all day for me. Like I said, it feels like I got a motor running inside me, and if I gotta sit still too long—like at church, or here waiting at the clinic, or even just at home on the couch—I start feeling all trapped in my body.

I’ll be trying to relax, but then I’m up walking around, messing with something, checking the door, moving a chair, whatever. Sometimes I don’t even know why I got up, I just know sitting there feels wrong. It gets in the way, yeah.
Do these feelings of restlessness and trouble focusing happen in different places—like at home, at work, and when you're out in public—or are they mostly in one specific place?

I’m not really sure how to separate it out like that. I mean, I notice it at home, sure, but that’s where I am most of the time anyway. When I’m out, like at the store or waiting somewhere, I can get antsy too, but then there’s people and noise and I start watching what’s going on, and—well, like last time I went to get groceries I forgot the one thing I went in for because I saw they moved the bread aisle, or maybe they didn’t move it, I don’t know.

So… I don’t know if it’s one place. It feels like it just kinda follows me, but I haven’t really sat down and tracked it or nothing.
When did you first start noticing these feelings of restlessness and trouble focusing? Were they something you experienced even when you were a kid, or did they start more recently?

Oh, that’s been… I mean, that goes way back. Back when I was a boy in school, they were always moving my seat around, trying to put me up front or away from other kids, ’cause I couldn’t stay put.

I’d talk when I wasn’t supposed to, blurt stuff out, and I’d be up out of my chair before class was even done. Got in trouble for that a lot. Teachers used to act like I was doing it on purpose, but I don’t know… I just felt like I had to move or say something. I remember one teacher had this little chart on the wall—well, I don’t remember what it was for exactly—but my name was always getting put up there. So yeah, it wasn’t just recent. It’s been since I was little.
